headline: US stocks trade mixed as small caps lead and tech weakens amid new Trump tariffs and hotter core PCE reinforcing December Fed hike expectations
raw_text:
- HP Inc. (HPQ) rises about 12% after fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS of $0.83 beats estimates, driven by 14% growth in its Personal Systems segment and tariff refunds
- Ambarella (AMBA) drops roughly 18% after issuing Q4 revenue guidance of $70–75 million, well below the $112 million consensus due to memory cost pressures
- Nutanix (NTNX) falls about 15% after CEO Rajiv Ramaswami announces he will step down once a successor is appointed, overshadowing Q1 revenue of $772 million that tops estimates
- Nvidia (NVDA) trades about 4% lower after S&P placed it on CreditWatch with negative implications citing governance and management concerns, with broader semiconductor weakness also pressuring Lam Research (LRCX) and Micron (MU)
- Major US indexes trade mixed, with the Dow Jones ($DJI) up about 0.6%, the Russell 2000 (IWM) climbing around 0.8%, the S&P 500 ($SPX) dipping slightly, and the Nasdaq 100 ($NDX) falling about 0.6% as investors rotate into small caps and value while technology lags
- Materials leads sector performance with gains near 2.5%, contrasting with an ongoing AI-driven selloff in technology names
- The Trump administration unveils tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU, and around a dozen other trading partners, citing excess industrial capacity and unfair practices
- October core PCE inflation prints at 3.3% versus the 3.2% consensus and 3.1% prior as the Fed notes inflation has not improved and third-quarter GDP is revised sharply higher, reinforcing expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December and helping stocks pare earlier losses during the session
